title: gRPC unary
summary: Unary calls against a reflection-enabled server. Includes an enterprise test plan (jobs starting ent-).
description: Load tests a gRPC server that has reflection turned on: a unary call and a call with a small payload. It shows per-call latency and throughput over HTTP/2 without needing the .proto files.

variables.name: target
variables.guide: host:port of the service, for example staging.example.com:50051. BLASTA runs in a container, so for a service on your own machine use host.docker.internal instead of localhost.

variables.name: method
variables.guide: The full gRPC method, for example /helloworld.Greeter/SayHello. `grpcurl -plaintext host:port list` lists services if reflection is enabled.

jobs.name: gRPC unary call
jobs.notes: Edit the payload for your message type. The payload is raw protobuf bytes as text, so simple messages are easiest.

jobs.name: gRPC small payload
jobs.notes: Lower rate to isolate connection overhead from per-call cost.

jobs.name: gRPC unary: 01 smoke
jobs.notes: Enterprise plan, step 1 of 10. One request a second for 30 seconds. Run this first, every time: it proves the address, credentials and headers are right and that the environment is up before any real load is applied. Gate: zero errors. Reference request: gRPC unary call.

jobs.name: gRPC unary: 02 baseline (20% load)
jobs.notes: Step 2 of 10. About a fifth of normal traffic for 5 minutes: the uncontended latency of this request. Every later result is judged against it, so record p50 and p95. Gate: at most 0.5% errors and the default latency targets. Reference request: gRPC unary call.

jobs.name: gRPC unary: 03 average load (SLO check)
jobs.notes: Step 3 of 10. Normal busy-hour traffic for 10 minutes. The rate is the reference job's rate: raise it to your measured production peak-hour rate. This is the run that proves (or breaks) your SLO. Gate: at most 1% errors, p95 and p99 inside the targets. Reference request: gRPC unary call.

jobs.name: gRPC unary: 04 peak load (2x average)
jobs.notes: Step 4 of 10. Twice the average for 10 minutes: the busiest hour of the year plus headroom. Latency may rise, but must stay in SLO; if it does not, you have no headroom. Gate: at most 2% errors, latency targets doubled. Reference request: gRPC unary call.

jobs.name: gRPC unary: 05 stress (ramp to 4x)
jobs.notes: Step 5 of 10. Ramps to four times average over 10 minutes, then holds for 2. Finds where it degrades and HOW: gracefully (latency rises, errors stay low) or badly (errors, timeouts, crashes, restarts). Observation only, no gate. Reference request: gRPC unary call.

jobs.name: gRPC unary: 06 spike (10x in 10 s)
jobs.notes: Step 6 of 10. Reaches ten times average within 10 seconds and holds for 2 minutes: a campaign email, a news link, a failover. Checks autoscaling, queue limits and load shedding. Gate: at most 5% errors, because shedding load is acceptable and crashing is not. Reference request: gRPC unary call.

jobs.name: gRPC unary: 07 recovery after the spike
jobs.notes: Step 7 of 10. Run IMMEDIATELY after the spike, at average load for 5 minutes. Latency and errors must return to the baseline from step 2. If they do not, something is stuck: queues, connection pools, GC, an autoscaler cool-down. Gate: same as average load. Reference request: gRPC unary call.

job.name: gRPC unary: 07 recovery after the spike

jobs.name: gRPC unary: 08 soak (1 hour at 60%)
jobs.notes: Step 8 of 10. One hour of steady load. Finds leaks and slow decay in memory, connections, file descriptors, disk, log volume and cache churn. Watch the resource graphs: any line that climbs and never flattens is a finding. Gate: at most 0.5% errors. Reference request: gRPC unary call.

jobs.name: gRPC unary: 09 breakpoint (find the ceiling)
jobs.notes: Step 9 of 10. Ramps to twenty times average over 20 minutes. Stop it when errors pass about 5%: the rate at that moment is your ceiling, and ceiling divided by peak is your capacity margin. Use a production-like environment, never production. Reference request: gRPC unary call.

jobs.name: gRPC unary: 10 resilience window (failover / deploy)
jobs.notes: Step 10 of 10. Average load for 15 minutes. About 5 minutes in, cause the event you are testing: kill a pod or node, fail over the database, roll out a new version, drain a zone. Errors in the window are your real availability loss. Gate: at most 1% errors overall; read the time series for how long the dip lasted. Reference request: gRPC unary call.

jobs.name: gRPC unary: connection storm (ramp to 10x)
jobs.notes: Ramps new connections per second to ten times normal: a fleet reconnecting after an outage, a deploy that restarts every pod, a network blip. Shows accept-queue, file descriptor and handshake limits. Reference request: gRPC unary call.
